question: Does curl preserve an existing HSTS destination and a symlink target until its replacement cache has been written successfully?

sources.name: curl issue 21610
sources.claim: Reports destination pre-truncation and symlink-target truncation in Curl_fopen and identifies the owning callers.

sources.name: curl current source
sources.claim: Current non-Windows Curl_fopen opens the final path with write/truncate mode before fstat and temporary-file creation.

sources.name: fopen optimize regression commit
sources.claim: Changed Curl_fopen from stat-before-open to open-before-fstat.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The symlink target remains 16 bytes and the destination symlink is handled without modifying the target.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The installed curl does not reproduce the symlink-target truncation mechanism.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The symlink target becomes shorter before the destination path becomes a regular HSTS file.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The installed curl reproduces final-path open/truncate before replacement.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: A 10,801-byte existing HSTS file remains intact when the child process is limited to 1,024-byte files.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The previous destination is preserved across a later persistence failure.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The existing HSTS file is replaced by a shorter file and no write error is reported separately from the transfer failure.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The previous destination is not protected by an atomic all-or-nothing persistence boundary.

stop_condition: Stop after two repeat runs establish or refute both installed-binary mechanisms; current-master candidate testing belongs to a promoted follow-up.
network_policy: No external network; one refused loopback connection to 127.0.0.1:1 per case.
